At the center, a long, rough‑hewn oak table holds a large parchment charter ruled faint red, goose quills, an ink horn, a penknife, a small brazier softening green and red wax, and silk cords. In the foreground, the close hands of a tonsured scribe press a bronze seal matrix into warm wax as a high church envoy in a gold‑embroidered chasuble and plain white mitre, crozier in hand, leans in; deacons in albs and dalmatics flank him. To the left, Portuguese envoys in 12th‑century dress—madder‑red and woad‑blue wool cloaks pinned with simple brooches over mail hauberks, leather belts with bronze buckles, conical nasal helmets and kite shields resting against the wall—watch with contained anticipation. To the right, Leónese representatives in rich but sober period tunics and patterned silks look on, hands poised over the table. Around them rise thick ashlar walls, semicircular arches, and a soot‑darkened barrel vault; capitals are carved with stylized vines and beasts, and the far apse bears faint frescoes of saints and a Pantocrator in earthy pigments. Worn flagstones, plank benches, a leather‑bound coffer, and woven rushes ground the space; incense haze and drifting dust catch the light, casting a hushed, momentous atmosphere. Malabar Coast, 1498: a humid late-morning landing on the beach at Calicut as a Portuguese fleet anchors offshore. In the foreground, a surf-wet longboat grinds onto pale sand; salt-stained oarsmen steady it while a small landing party steps ashore—sunburned sailors in faded wool doublets and hose, a few soldiers in quilted brigandines and simple steel sallet caps, one gripping a matchlock and another a halberd. An officer in a dark velvet jerkin with slashed sleeves cradles a rolled sea chart; from a belt hangs a polished brass astrolabe catching hard tropical light. A standard-bearer holds a white banner marked with a red cross, its linen snapping in the monsoon breeze. An open gift coffer reveals coils of scarlet cloth, strings of glass beads, and lumps of red coral. To the right beneath a low palm-frond canopy stand local officials and traders: a high-caste administrator in a white cotton mundu with a gold border, bare chest gleaming with oil, sandalwood paste on his brow; beside him a Muslim merchant in a clean white robe and cap, and an Arab trader in a wrapped turban. A Brahmin scribe crouches on a reed mat, incising palm-leaf manuscripts with a stylus. Nair guards flank the group with round lacquered shields and curved swords, spears upright; an attendant shades the official with a woven parasol. Between the groups lie stacked cane baskets of black pepper, heaps of ginger and cinnamon quills, coils of coir rope, and tarred casks; the flank of a caparisoned elephant edges into frame, brass bells at its neck. Middle distance: fishermen haul a net in the shore break while, beyond the surf line, three towering naus/carracks ride at anchor—tar-dark hulls with high forecastles and sterncastles, square sails emblazoned with red crosses, a lateen mizzen taut in the breeze; a smaller caravel and lateen-rigged dhows tack across indigo water. The shoreline behind is lined with laterite walls and low warehouses of carved teak and clay tiles, gabled Kerala roofs stepping up toward a temple with layered tiled eaves amid leaning coconut palms. Light is hot and hazy, humidity softening edges; glitter dances on wavelets, dust motes float in slanting sun under the canopy. Lisbon, 1 November 1755, All Saints’ Day morning: a wide, cinematic street-and-waterfront scene captured from a slightly elevated angle beneath a cracked arcade, looking out toward the Tagus. In the foreground, shattered blue-and-white azulejo tiles, splintered timber beams, and chunks of pale limestone litter broken cobbles; a toppled wooden saint from a gilded church retable lies amid smoking candles and torn processional banners. Survivors surge through dust: priests in black cassocks and birettas guiding the wounded, nuns in white wimples, dockworkers in coarse linen and wool caps hauling at debris, ladies in embroidered bodices, lace fichus, and mantillas clutching children, and men in justaucorps, waistcoats, breeches, stockings, buckled shoes, and tricornes, faces powdered with ash. At mid-ground, a Baroque church façade with volutes and a cracked pediment sheds stucco; its bell tower lists as a bronze bell swings free. Across the square, the arcaded riverfront palace buckles—wrought-iron balconies twisted, terracotta roof tiles cascading—while narrow lanes of whitewashed houses with overhanging eaves gape open, revealing splintered staircases and gilded woodwork within.
